title: Agent tries to update a ticket for Susan

actors.label: AI agent
actors.description: An MCP client, e.g. a coding assistant

story.title: You asked the agent
story.what: Susan asked the agent to work with ticket 42.
story.why: The agent has no rights of its own here. It acts strictly on Susan's behalf.
story.matters: Every agent action traces back to a real person and inherits that person's limits.

story.title: The gateway brokered the request to the identity provider
story.what: The gateway presented Susan's identity and the agent's own credentials, asking for an Identity Assertion JWT (ID-JAG).
story.why: An agent can't mint its own access. Only the identity provider issues tokens, and only after evaluating policy.
story.matters: The exchange is the checkpoint: every agent action passes through policy before it can touch a resource.

story.title: The identity provider minted a narrow token
story.what: A token for the ticket API was issued, but the agent's connection is limited below Susan, so it carries only tickets.read.
story.why: The token is the intersection of what the user may do and what this agent may do.
story.matters: Even though Susan may update tickets, this agent may not. The limit is in the token itself.

story.title: The ticket API refused the call (403)
story.what: The API checked the token, found no tickets.write scope, and refused.
story.why: Resources enforce scope on every call.
story.matters: The agent limit is not a policy note. It is a machine-checked refusal at the resource.

subtitle: Cross App Access: ID-JAG token exchange through an MCP gateway

outcome.headline: ✕ REFUSED: AGENT LIMITED
outcome.detail: A token was minted, but the agent's connection is limited below Susan, so it lacked tickets.write and the API refused.
outcome.caption: token minted but narrower than the user · API refused (403)

tokens.label: Delegated access token
tokens.note: sub is the user; act.sub is the agent acting on their behalf (RFC 8693 actor claim).
